handfixes.summary: --dry-run returns its request preview before authHeader() runs, using only the already-cached Authorization value, so a dry run never calls the OAuth token endpoint.
handfixes.why: The generated doInternal resolved auth (authHeader, which mints a client_credentials token on a cold cache) BEFORE the c.DryRun branch, so `--dry-run` sent the Access ID and password to the token URL and cached the minted token - a 'no request sent' preview that made a real login. Found by the build pane (cli-factory/watchguard NOTES.md) and reproduced at onboarding 2026-10-15: with WATCHGUARD_TOKEN_URL pointed at a recording server, `accounts list-managed --dry-run` hit POST /oauth/token before the fix and made zero requests after it (isolate --dry-run and accounts health --dry-run too). Press template client.go.tmpl; likely fleet-wide for client-credentials connectors. A reprint regenerates client.go and reverts it while go build and go test stay green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press fix: client.go.tmpl should branch on DryRun before authHeader().

asserts.contains: return c.dryRun(method, targetURL, path, params, bodyBytes, headerOverrides, dryRunAuth)

handfixes.summary: Secret-named JSON keys (any key containing password, passphrase, secret, psk, pvt_key, private key, pfx/pkcs12, api key, activation/license key or activation/verification code, any key ending in token, and otp/p12; case-insensitive; booleans and nulls exempt) are dropped at any depth before any row reaches the local store (generic blob, typed columns and FTS index, via the single mergeIncomingResourceData choke point), and an HTTP response that carries one is never written to the response cache. Endpoint Security installer responses (enrollment download links) are never cached and are stored as an empty object. Helper: internal/cliutil/secretfields.go.
handfixes.why: WatchGuard Firebox Management GETs return live secrets in ordinary rows: BOVPN tunnels carry psk/psk_encrypted, certificates carry pvt_key and password, networks carry PPPoE/Dynamic DNS passwords, Wi-Fi passphrases and DHCP auth tokens, users and content filtering carry passwords, and the activation API returns activationKey. Found at onboarding (2026-10-15) by scanning the spec's 2xx response schemas, then proven with a sentinel mock: a default `sync` plus list/get of each resource wrote every sentinel into data.db (typed psk column included) and 11 response-cache files. With the hooks: zero sentinels on disk while the rows still sync. internal/store/secret_fields_test.go fails (20 'secret persisted' findings) with the store hook reverted; internal/cliutil/secretfields_test.go covers the cache-side detection. A reprint regenerates store.go and client.go and silently drops both hooks while go build and go test stay green. Codex review (2026-10-15): allocation responses carry software license keys in serialOrLicense (a field that also holds Firebox serials and distinguishes allocation rows, so it stays in the mirror, documented in governance.md); no license allocation response is cached any more.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Needs a press feature: an x-secret / writeOnly-aware store projection that never persists credential fields; no spec extension expresses it today.

handfixes.summary: An env-sourced WATCHGUARD_BASE_URL, WATCHGUARD_TOKEN_URL or WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNT_ID is marked as an env override in config.Load, and configForSave writes the file's own value back instead, so config.toml never captures the override and unsetting the variable restores the default.
handfixes.why: Reproduced at onboarding (2026-10-15): after one run with WATCHGUARD_BASE_URL/TOKEN_URL/ACCOUNT_ID set, config.toml held base_url, token_url and [template_vars] accountId. Unsetting the variables then had no effect: requests kept going to the old region host, every token mint sent the Access ID and password to the old token URL, and requests kept the old account ID. Same generator defect threatdown recorded. internal/config/env_urls_test.go fails with the restore lines removed. A reprint regenerates config.go and reverts it while go build and go test stay green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: configForSave should restore every env-overridden field, not only credentials.

handfixes.summary: The root command's Short and Long help open with "WatchGuard Cloud CLI" instead of the generated "Watchguard CLI".

handfixes.summary: Every variable the binaries read is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb user_config + server.mcp_config.env), server.json (MCP Registry) and the three mcp-install.md env blocks. Beyond the Access ID, password, API key and account ID these are the optional WATCHGUARD_BASE_URL, WATCHGUARD_TOKEN_URL (regions), WATCHGUARD_AUDIENCE, WATCHGUARD_OAUTH_SCOPE, WATCHGUARD_USER_AGENT, WATCHGUARD_MCP_READ_ONLY, WATCHGUARD_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, blank (not placeholders) in mcp-install.md. WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNT_ID is not marked secret on either channel.
handfixes.why: check_env_schema failed the onboard with 8 read-but-undeclared variables, so a Claude Desktop install could never select the EMEA or APAC region, pin one customer, or run read-only; server.json marked the account ID secret while the manifest did not. onboard.py --resume re-vendors manifest.json from the press source, which declares only the four required values, so a re-onboard drops the rest while the build stays green.

handfixes.summary: Generated SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md carry corrections for this CLI: the exit-code table documents firebox-transactions wait's 8 (failed) and 9 (still running), the env table names WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNT_ID (not WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNTID) plus the region and audience variables, AGENTS.md examples use real commands and a low-entropy device ID, and AGENTS.md says writes send without confirmation. guide.md also carries the Windows forms main gave every other connector guide in #390: the %USERPROFILE% default config path and a PowerShell $env:WATCHGUARD_HOME block.
handfixes.why: The generated docs named a wrong env var (WATCHGUARD_ACCOUNTID), a wrong config path and `auth-status`, used <command> placeholders, and documented exit 8 only as 'async job not finished' - for firebox-transactions wait it means the deployment FAILED. The build pane's postgen_docs.py applies the doc fixes after every generate; onboard.py --resume re-vendors SKILL.md, AGENTS.md and guide.md from the source and would drop the msp-skills edits. handfixes.summary: A client-credentials token is saved with token_binding, a fingerprint of the Access ID, scope and token URL it was minted for (config.TokenBindingFor). A process whose Access ID, WATCHGUARD_OAUTH_SCOPE or token URL gives a different fingerprint mints its own token, and when it has no password to mint with it fails with exit 4 instead of using the cached token. An environment Access ID never pairs with the password saved for a different one, repeated saves keep the saved pair and API key, and a [headers] Authorization entry is never sent. The WatchGuard-API-Key is not part of the binding.
handfixes.why: Reproduced at onboarding (2026-10-15): with a token cached for Access ID RW, a process with WATCHGUARD_CLIENT_ID=RO and its own password made no token request and sent RW's token; a process with only a different scope also rode it. WatchGuard issues separate read-write and read-only Access IDs, so a read-only setup silently ran with read-write rights. Ported from threatdown's token-bound-to-client (same press 4.33.5 template). Tests fail on revert: TestCachedTokenBoundToClientAndScope, TestCachedTokenBindingFailsClosed, TestReadOnlyAccessIDNeverRidesReadWriteToken (end to end), TestConfiguredHeadersNeverCarryAuthorization, TestEnvClientIDNeverPairsWithSavedSecret, TestRepeatedSavesKeepSavedClientPair, TestAuthLoginSavesThePairItUsed, TestBoundElsewhereReadExitsWithAuthCode, TestDoctorReportsTokenBoundElsewhere and more. A reprint regenerates client.go, config.go, credentials.go and auth.go and silently reverts it while go build and go test stay green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Generator defect: the press's client-credentials cache should key the token on the client ID and scope.

asserts.contains: func TokenBindingFor(clientID string, scope string, tokenURL string) string
persisted.ClientID, persisted.ClientSecret, persisted.WatchguardApiKey = savedID, savedSecret, savedKey

handfixes.summary: `auth status` and doctor share client.AuthState: a complete Access ID + password pair (env or saved) counts as authenticated, and a cached token bound to a different Access ID, scope or token URL with no password to mint a replacement reports authenticated:false, token_bound_elsewhere:true and exits 4. Any <...> value and any unresolved ${...} template is a placeholder, an env placeholder error names the variable (including WATCHGUARD_API_KEY), auth login refuses placeholders, and doctor reports a rejected token request as a credentials error.
handfixes.why: Before the fix a fresh home with a valid env pair printed authenticated:false, and a saved read-write login with a read-only env Access ID and no password printed authenticated:true while every call failed. Ported from threatdown. Tests fail on revert: TestAuthStatusTracksTokenBinding, TestAuthStatusAndDoctorAgreeOnEnvPairs, TestDoctorReportsRejectedMintAsCredentials, TestPlaceholderErrorNamesTheEnvVar, TestAnglePlaceholdersAreNotCredentials, TestAuthLoginRefusesPlaceholders.

handfixes.summary: Every refresh hint the binary gives (the stale-store hint and doctor's stale-cache hint) names `sync --full`, not a bare `sync`.
handfixes.why: No WatchGuard resource syncs incrementally, so a bare sync re-walks everything but never prunes, and a retired Firebox stays in the mirror (and in firebox-devices changes / firmware-lag). `sync --full` costs no extra requests. TestRefreshGuidanceNamesFullSync and TestDoctorStaleHintNamesFullSync fail on revert.

handfixes.summary: SKILL.md carries a 'Safety for agents' section naming the credential reads, the endpoint-affecting and configuration writes, WATCHGUARD_MCP_READ_ONLY and the fan-out exit codes, its title is 'WatchGuard Cloud Claude Code Skill', and its description leads with 'Use when the user asks'.
handfixes.why: The generated SKILL.md never told an agent which reads print pre-shared keys and private keys or that every write sends without confirmation, and its title said 'Printing Press CLI'. onboard.py --resume re-vendors SKILL.md from the press source and drops all three.

handfixes.summary: listRows and incidentRows require the collection to be a JSON list of objects: {"data":null}, a scalar, an object or a list of non-objects is a failed read, never zero devices, endpoints or incidents. A {key: X} wrapper row (the [{"data":{...},"total_items":N}] form) whose X is null or a scalar is a failed read too, in listRows and in incidentRows' top-level-list branch. firebox-transactions wait applies the same rule: wait --device reads the transaction list through listRows, and firstObject never skips a malformed wrapper row to reach the row after it. Single-record reads go through asMapsStrict, which fails on a null or scalar row at any wrapper depth; firebox-transactions wait <id> reports such a body as a failed read (exit 5), not "not found", and a list answer must contain the requested id. An object that carries its own id is a record, never an envelope, even with a "data" field (a status alone does not make one: {"status":"success","data":...} is an envelope) (the documented certificate-install and deployment transaction records); a top-level null or scalar is a failed read; and a single-row answer naming another transaction is a failed read.
handfixes.why: Codex read-only review round 1 (2026-10-15): listRows checked only that the key existed, so {"data":null} or {"data":"unavailable"} became an empty fleet and accounts health reported zero counts with complete:true and exit 0; incidentRows accepted {"items":null} the same way. Companion to fanout-partial-data-exit. TestListRowsRejectsMalformedCollections fails on revert. Codex read-only review round 2 (2026-10-15): asMaps silently dropped wrapped null/scalar rows, so [{"data":null}] or [{"items":null}] still read as zero rows; wrappedRowsErr mirrors asMaps and fails those reads. The new TestListRowsRejectsMalformedCollections cases fail on revert. Codex read-only review round 3 (2026-10-15): wait --device read the list through raw asMaps, so [{"data":null},{"data":{...complete}}] picked an older finished transaction and exited 0. TestTransactionsWaitRejectsMalformedRows fails on revert of either the listRows call or the firstObject guard. Adversarial round 6 (2026-10-15): the one-level firstObject pre-check still skipped {"data":{"data":[{"data":null},{...complete}]}} to an older transaction (exit 0), a malformed by-ID body read as exit 3, and a two-row by-ID answer used its first row. TestTransactionsWaitRejectsMalformedRows fails on revert of each piece. Adversarial round 7 and Codex round 5 (2026-10-15): asMapsStrict unwrapped a top-level record's own "data" field (wait on a certificate-install record exited 5, a deployment record with data exited 3), a top-level null read as not found, and [{"id":"old",...}] for wait new exited 0. TestTransactionsWaitRejectsMalformedRows fails on revert of each.

handfixes.summary: A software license key in an allocation row's serialOrLicense is replaced by a one-way fingerprint (license: plus 16 hex) before the row is persisted, indexed or tailed; Firebox and access point serial numbers (productName firebox, fireboxRetention, accessPoint) are kept. The row's declared productName decides, never the value's shape; a row with no productName is treated as a key. On the request side, a software license key sent in serialOrLicense (allocations allocate, import) is a request secret: it is withheld from error echoes and masked in the --dry-run preview; a Firebox or access point serial stays readable. The same holds for a key in the query string (allocations deallocate sends serialOrLicense as a query parameter; the MCP server builds it into the path): the request URL's query feeds the secret set, the --dry-run preview prints [redacted], and an error or transport error shows the URL with its query withheld.
handfixes.why: Codex read-only review round 1 (2026-10-15): the secret-field policy already classes license keys as credentials, but serialOrLicense was exempted for row identity and the typed allocations column stored software license keys in plaintext. allocations reconcile reads live rows, so the mirror fingerprint changes nothing it matches. governance.md, README.md and page.json describe the behavior. TestLicenseKeysFingerprinted and TestLicenseKeysNeverPersisted fail on revert. Codex read-only review round 2 (2026-10-15): requestSecrets and redactBody used only the secret-name list, which excludes serialOrLicense, so an API error echoing the key or a --dry-run preview printed it. TestLicenseKeyNeverEchoedOrPreviewed fails on revert. Codex round 3 and adversarial round 5 (2026-10-15) both found the query-string path: deallocate --dry-run printed the key and a 400 echo or a transport error showed it. TestLicenseKeyInQueryNeverEchoedOrPreviewed fails on revert of querySecrets, the transport URL withholding, the dry-run mask, displayURL, or urlQuery.

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard compares trustees by SID, resolving SDDL aliases through the OS, so the built-in Administrator (RID 500, rendered as LA) can save and load credentials
handfixes.why: Press 4.30.2+ creds_perms_eval.go compared the SDDL text of the token file's owner and ACE trustees against the process's SID string. The SDDL converter renders the built-in local Administrator (RID 500) as the alias LA, so that account's own ACE never matched: `auth set-token` exited 1 with `token file DACL grants access to a non-owner principal (LA)` and every read refused the file. Reproduced 2026-10-15 on the published fortinet-cli 0.1.0, installed with the README one-liner on a windows-latest runner (whoami S-1-5-21-...-500). The fix resolves each trustee to its SID (fixed aliases from a table, machine-relative ones like LA through ConvertStringSidToSid, kept only when the converter renders that SID back to the same alias) and compares SIDs. The allow-list is unchanged (current user, BUILTIN\Administrators, SYSTEM): an owner or allow-ACE trustee that is any other principal, a broad group, or unresolvable is still refused. A reprint from an unfixed press silently restores the string compare while unit tests stay green on every non-Windows host. Ported to watchguard from main's #391 (the generated files were byte-identical before the fix).

handfixes.summary: the Windows token-file guard checks the DACL section's framing, so a NULL DACL is refused in the form Windows actually renders it, flags first (D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL), and DACL text that does not frame as flags plus complete six-field ACEs is refused rather than skipped
handfixes.why: Press creds_perms_eval.go refused a NULL DACL only when the DACL section began with NO_ACCESS_CONTROL. SDDL puts DACL flags (P, AI, AR) first, and a real NULL DACL on Windows Server 2025 renders as O:<owner>D:PAINO_ACCESS_CONTROL (measured on a windows-latest runner, 2026-10-15), so the guard found no ACEs to inspect and accepted a world-accessible token file. That was already a hole for every ordinary account; for the built-in Administrator the owner-alias mismatch happened to refuse it, so resolving LA (windows-sddl-alias-sid-compare) without this fix would have widened the hole. The DACL section's framing is now checked: its flags must be drawn from P/AI/AR/NO_ACCESS_CONTROL, an empty DACL followed by a SACL section ends at that section, and the ACE list must be complete, un-nested (...) groups of exactly six fields. Unknown flags, an unclosed or nested group, stray text, or a wrong field count is refused (fail-closed). ACE flags and rights are not validated; they do not change which principal an allow ACE names. Ported to watchguard from main's #391 (the generated files were byte-identical before the fix).
